Chapter 4: Choosing Platforms and Methods to Share the Message
Once you've built up your credibility, the next big question is—how do you actually get your message out there? These days, there's a whole world of platforms and methods, each with its own perks and possibilities. The trick is to pick the channels that really fit your strengths, speak to your audience, and suit the heart of your message.
So, what are your main options when it comes to sharing your expertise? Let’s break it down:
You can write and publish—think books, articles, or blogs. There’s public speaking, like leading seminars, workshops, or speaking at conferences. Coaching and consulting work really well too, whether that’s one-on-one or in small groups. And, of course, there are online products and courses—videos, webinars, digital downloads. Plus, social media and content marketing, which covers everything from posts and podcasts to live streams.
Each of these platforms does something a little different. For example, writing a book helps you establish authority and gives people a resource they can return to again and again. Speaking lets you connect in real time and build real relationships. Coaching is all about that personal touch, while online courses make it possible to reach folks all around the world without leaving your home.
Now, how do you decide which mix of platforms is right for you? Start by thinking honestly about what you enjoy and where your strengths lie. Are you more comfortable writing, or do you light up in front of a crowd? Next, look at your audience—where do they spend their time? What do they like to engage with? Also, think about the kind of transformation you’re promising. Are you aiming for deep, personal breakthroughs, or are you sharing practical tips with a broad audience? And don’t forget your resources—how much time, budget, and tech know-how do you have?
Here’s a practical tip: start simple. Pick one or two platforms that feel the most natural, and focus your energy there. If you love writing, maybe launch a blog or regular newsletter. If you get energized by live interaction, consider hosting workshops or webinars. As you gain confidence and get more comfortable, you can always branch out into new formats.
There’s also a huge advantage in repurposing your content. Imagine you’ve just run a great seminar—why not turn the main points into a series of blog posts, a downloadable guide, or even a video series? This way, you get more mileage out of your ideas and reach different segments of your audience.
To keep everything running smoothly, it helps to map out a simple content plan. Outline the topics you want to cover, decide on the formats you’ll use, and set a schedule for publishing or presenting. Staying organized and intentional makes it so much easier to keep up your momentum and nurture a loyal following.
Above all, focus on creating value-driven content. Put your audience’s needs and interests front and center—not just your products or services. Aim to educate, inspire, or solve a problem. If you do that, people will come away feeling like they’ve truly gained something.
Over time, as your message spreads and your audience grows, you’ll notice new doors opening. Maybe you’ll get invited to speak, receive requests for coaching, or find opportunities to team up with other experts. The most important thing is to stay flexible, listen to your audience, and keep your commitment to serving others through the platforms you’ve chosen.
